for_the_reviewer:
THE TWO FAULTS, AND WHERE TO PRESS.

Fault 4. I reproduced your count before touching anything - your program, written again from the criterion's words, over the same 96: 79 of 96 with a Part/Mark table, 7 with colliding keys, your seven reports and your duplicate keys exactly. Both your clauses are in, and the fixed rule gives 0 of 79. The thing to press is the half of clause (1) you left open: 'a separator and more text'. My first reading - a closed list of separator characters - reverted 52 of 750 rows, including 'P4. “Known integer” means efficiently generatable/provable.' and 'P2 +1 segment per ACK', because a curly quote and a plus were not on the list. It is now 'any run of characters that are not letters or digits', which reverts 28 of 750, every one a collision or one of three quotation-led labels. Both forms are written into marking-plan 14.1 because the discarded one is the more instructive. The second place to press: clause (2) makes a row's key depend on which OTHER rows the marker read as belonging to the part-by-part section, so two markers who disagree about the section's boundary can now disagree about a key neither of them disputes. That is the patch's bill and I have said where it lands.

Fault 25. Your three clauses are in, with two additions named as mine: the decidable form of the lead-in (an emphasised or bracketed run whose text carries the word 'rival', so '- **Add a job.**' is left alone), and a fallback for a report with no whole-explanation section, without which clause (2) leaves such a report with no sentence at all. Your four cold reports now give one value each and they are in a table in 14.2 with what each admitted before. The one judgement left on runs/I1-m1.json is the BUILT test, not the naming rule, and I left it alone on purpose.

THE COUNT THAT HAS FAILED, and I am not going to write my way round it. W3 P3.4 allows at most one field a second rewording.
